- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., 0.0 to 0.5), model overreacts to short-term volatility; apply smoothing filter to dampen 3–5 day momentum.
- In periods of high volatility or event-driven context (e.g., policy change, auction), model underestimates downside risk; add 3–5% buffer for downward correction.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day mean by 2–5% in sentiment-neutral or mildly positive environments; adjust mean reversion target to 1–2% below historical 30-day average.
- When sentiment turns negative after a positive trend, model fails to reverse quickly; force a 2–3 day lagged correction with 10–15% downward adjustment.
- In low-sentiment, low-volatility periods, model tends to underestimate true range; widen forecast band by 5–10% to account for hidden volatility.
